# Q3: chain-2 COUNT
# dataset: social
# Friends of friends; always 9 x persons solutions because every out-degree is 3.
PREFIX : <http://example.org/social/>
SELECT (COUNT(*) AS ?count)
WHERE {
  ?a :knows ?b .
  ?b :knows ?c .
}

queries.title: selective chain-3 from a constant
queries.text:
# Q4: selective chain-3 from a constant
# dataset: social
# Three hops from :p123 (exactly 27 solutions, duplicates included).
PREFIX : <http://example.org/social/>
SELECT ?a ?b ?c
WHERE {
  :p123 :knows ?a .
  ?a :knows ?b .
  ?b :knows ?c .
}

queries.title: OPTIONAL with a type check inside
FILTER(?a > 90)
queries.text:
# Q6: FILTER(?a > 90)
# dataset: social
# Selective integer range (about 0.7% of the persons).
PREFIX : <http://example.org/social/>
SELECT ?x ?a
WHERE {
  ?x :age ?a .
  FILTER(?a > 90)
}

queries.title: REGEX on names
queries.text:
# Q7: REGEX on names
# dataset: social
# Case-insensitive anchored regular expression over every name.
PREFIX : <http://example.org/social/>
SELECT ?x ?n
WHERE {
  ?x :name ?n .
  FILTER(REGEX(?n, "^person 1[0-9]*7$", "i"))
}

queries.title: GROUP BY + COUNT + ORDER BY DESC LIMIT 10
queries.text:
# Q8: GROUP BY + COUNT + ORDER BY DESC LIMIT 10
# dataset: social
# ordered: true
# The ten most populous cities; ?c breaks ties so the order is total.
PREFIX : <http://example.org/social/>
SELECT ?c (COUNT(?x) AS ?n)
WHERE {
  ?x :city ?c .
}
GROUP BY ?c
ORDER BY DESC(?n) ?c
LIMIT 10

queries.title: ORDER BY DESC(?age) ?x LIMIT 10
queries.text:
# Q9: ORDER BY DESC(?age) ?x LIMIT 10
# dataset: social
# ordered: true
# Top-k over an integer property; ?x breaks ties so the order is total.
PREFIX : <http://example.org/social/>
SELECT ?x ?age
WHERE {
  ?x :age ?age .
}
ORDER BY DESC(?age) ?x
LIMIT 10

queries.title: DISTINCT over a join
queries.text:
# Q10: DISTINCT over a join
# dataset: social
# (home city, friend's class) pairs: at most 10 x cities rows out of 3 x persons join rows.
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX : <http://example.org/social/>
SELECT DISTINCT ?c ?cls
WHERE {
  ?x :knows ?y .
  ?x :city ?c .
  ?y rdf:type ?cls .
}

BSBM offers: price range + date filter + ORDER BY price LIMIT 10
queries.text:
# Q17: BSBM offers: price range + date filter + ORDER BY price LIMIT 10
# dataset: bsbm
# ordered: true
# Prices mix xsd:decimal (some non-canonical, e.g. "12.50") and xsd:integer but never
# compare equal across the two, and ?offer breaks ties, so the order is total.
PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
PREFIX bsbm: <http://example.org/bsbm/vocabulary/>
SELECT ?offer ?price ?vendor ?product ?validTo
WHERE {
  ?offer bsbm:price ?price ;
         bsbm:validTo ?validTo ;
         bsbm:vendor ?vendor ;
         bsbm:product ?product .
  FILTER(?price >= 500 && ?price <= 1000)
  FILTER(?validTo >= "2008-06-01T00:00:00"^^xsd:dateTime)
}
ORDER BY ?price ?offer
LIMIT 10
